must_remember: A symmetric square wave alternating between $-V$ and $+V$ is an odd function, leading to zero cosine coefficients ($a_n = 0$).
Only odd harmonics ($\omega, 3\omega, 5\omega, \dots$) are present in a symmetric square wave due to half-wave antisymmetry.
The amplitude of the $n$-th harmonic in a square wave's Fourier series is given by $A_n = \frac{4V}{n\pi}$.
The RMS value of a symmetric square wave oscillating between $-V$ and $+V$ is equal to $V$.
The Gibbs phenomenon refers to the constant $\approx 9\%$ overshoot and ripples that occur near points of discontinuity when using a finite Fourier series.

glossary.meaning: A periodic waveform that alternates equally between $-V$ and $+V$ with a 50% duty cycle.
A function satisfying $f(-t) = -f(t)$, resulting in a Fourier series containing only sine terms.
A property where $f(t + T/2) = -f(t)$, which eliminates all even harmonics from the frequency spectrum.
The non-uniform convergence and persistent overshoot ($\approx 9\%$) of a Fourier series near a jump discontinuity.
Relates the total average power of a periodic signal to the sum of the powers of its individual harmonic components.
